apiVersion.description:
APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.
Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and
may reject unrecognized values.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources

kind.description:
Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.
Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to.
Cannot be updated.
In CamelCase.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds

spec.description:
NodeClassSpec is the top level specification for the AWS Karpenter Provider.
This will contain configuration necessary to launch instances in AWS.

advancedCompute.description: AdvancedCompute enables the configuration of compute behavior on Auto nodes, such as hugepage reservations.

hugepages.description: Hugepages configures explicit hugepage reservations on the node.

pages.description: Pages is a list of hugepage size and count pairs to reserve on each node.

items.description: HugePageEntry defines a single hugepage reservation.

count.description: Count is the number of hugepages of this size to reserve.

size.description: Size is the hugepage size to reserve.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: hugepages size must be unique

transparent.description:
Transparent configures transparent hugepages (THP) on the node. THP is a kernel-wide policy
rather than an allocatable resource, so it does not affect scheduling or node capacity.

defrag.description:
Defrag controls how aggressively the kernel compacts memory to satisfy a THP allocation.
Setting Enabled to "never" forces defrag to "never" in the kernel, so any other value is
rejected in that case. Defaults to the kernel default ("madvise") when unset.

enabled.description:
Enabled controls the THP allocation policy. "always" applies THP system-wide, "madvise"
applies it only to regions that opt in via madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE), and "never" disables it.
Defaults to the kernel default ("madvise") when unset.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: defrag cannot be enabled when enabled is 'never'

kernel.description: Kernel groups Linux-kernel-scoped configuration on the node.

sysctl.description:
Sysctl configures kernel sysctls on the node. Property names exactly match the
name of the underlying sysctl.

fs.aio-max-nr.description: The maximum number of asynchronous I/O requests.

fs.inotify.max_user_instances.description: The maximum number of inotify instances per real user ID.

fs.inotify.max_user_watches.description: The maximum number of inotify watches per real user ID.

fs.nr_open.description: The maximum number of file handles a process can allocate.

kernel.perf_event_paranoid.description: Controls unprivileged access to performance event systems.

net.core.netdev_max_backlog.description: The maximum number of packets queued on the INPUT side per CPU.

net.core.rmem_max.description: The maximum receive socket buffer size, in bytes.

net.core.somaxconn.description: The maximum value for the backlog argument in the listen syscall.

net.core.wmem_max.description: The maximum send socket buffer size, in bytes.

net.ipv4.neigh.default.gc_thresh1.description: Minimum ARP-cache entries before garbage collection can run.

net.ipv4.neigh.default.gc_thresh2.description: Soft maximum number of ARP-cache entries.

net.ipv4.neigh.default.gc_thresh3.description: Hard maximum number of ARP-cache entries.

net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control.description: The TCP congestion-control algorithm for new connections.

net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout.description:
The length of time, in seconds, an orphaned (no longer referenced by any application)
connection will remain in the FIN_WAIT_2 state before it is aborted at the local end.

net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time.description: How often, in seconds, TCP sends out keepalive messages when keepalive is enabled.

net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog.description:
The maximum number of outstanding SYN requests that are allowed. Requests beyond this
value are dropped by the kernel.

net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse.description:
Enable reuse of TIME-WAIT sockets for new connections when it is safe from a protocol
viewpoint. Valid values are 0 (disable), 1 (global enable), or 2 (enable for loopback only).

user.max_user_namespaces.description:
The maximum number of user namespaces creatable by a user. A value of 0 disables user
namespaces.

vm.dirty_background_ratio.description:
Percent of available memory at which kernel flusher threads begin
writing dirty pages back to disk.

vm.dirty_expire_centisecs.description: Hundredths of a second before a dirty page becomes eligible for writeback.

vm.dirty_ratio.description: Percent of available memory at which writing programs are forced to block on writes.

vm.dirty_writeback_centisecs.description: Hundredths of a second between flusher-thread invocations.

vm.max_map_count.description: The maximum number of memory map areas a single process may have.

vm.swappiness.description: Relative IO cost of swapping vs. filesystem paging.

vm.watermark_scale_factor.description: Memory reclaim watermark ratio in fractions of 10,000.

kubelet.description: Kubelet contains kubelet configuration overrides for Auto Mode nodes.

allowedUnsafeSysctls.description:
AllowedUnsafeSysctls is a list of unsafe sysctls (or namespaced patterns ending in "*")
that pods scheduled on this node are permitted to set.

cpuManager.description:
CpuManager configures the kubelet CPU manager policy.
When policy is "static", whole-core CPU pinning is enabled for guaranteed QoS pods.

policy.description: Policy is the CPU manager policy. "static" enables whole-core pinning for guaranteed QoS pods.

policyOptions.description:
PolicyOptions is a list of CPU manager policy options to enable. Only valid when policy is
"static". strict-cpu-reservation requires the CPUManagerPolicyBetaOptions kubelet feature gate.

items.description:
CPUManagerPolicyOption is a supported kubelet CPU manager policy option. Limited to the options the
Bottlerocket settings SDK supports.

eviction.description: Eviction configures kubelet eviction thresholds for resource pressure signals.

additionalProperties.description: EvictionThreshold is a string representing a percentage (e.g. "10%") or absolute quantity (e.g. "100Mi").

hard.description:
Hard eviction thresholds. When a signal crosses its threshold, pods are immediately evicted.
Valid keys: memory.available, nodefs.available, nodefs.inodesFree, imagefs.available, imagefs.inodesFree, pid.available.
Values may be a percentage (e.g. "10%") or an absolute quantity (e.g. "100Mi").

maxPodGracePeriod.description:
MaxPodGracePeriod is the maximum allowed grace period (in seconds) to use when terminating
pods in response to soft eviction thresholds being met. A value of 0 means each pod's
terminationGracePeriodSeconds is used.

additionalProperties.description: EvictionThreshold is a string representing a percentage (e.g. "10%") or absolute quantity (e.g. "100Mi").

soft.description:
Soft eviction thresholds. Pods are evicted after the signal remains past its threshold for the configured grace period.
Same key/value format as Hard.

SoftGracePeriod maps eviction signal names to duration strings (e.g. "1m30s") defining
how long a signal must exceed its soft threshold before eviction occurs.
Required when soft eviction thresholds are set.

idsPerPod.description:
IdsPerPod sets the number of UIDs/GIDs kubelet allocates to each pod's user namespace.
Requires advancedCompute.kernel.sysctl.user.max_user_namespaces to be set to a positive value.

logging.description: Logging configures container log rotation settings.

containerLogMaxFiles.description:
ContainerLogMaxFiles is the maximum number of rotated container log files to retain per container.
Total log retention per container = containerLogMaxSize x containerLogMaxFiles.

containerLogMaxSize.description: ContainerLogMaxSize is the maximum size of a container log file before it is rotated (e.g. "10Mi", "50Mi", "1Gi").

maxPods.description:
MaxPods overrides the maximum number of pods that can run on a node.
At runtime, this is clamped to min(maxPods, available IPs for the instance type).

podPidsLimit.description:
PodPidsLimit sets the maximum number of process IDs (PIDs) per pod.
A value of -1 disables the limit entirely.

singleProcessOOMKill.description:
SingleProcessOOMKill, if true, prevents the memory.oom.group flag from being set for
container cgroups. This causes processes in the container to be OOM killed individually
instead of as a group, aligning behavior with cgroups v1.

topologyManager.description:
TopologyManager configures the kubelet topology manager policy.
Controls NUMA-aware resource alignment for pods.

policy.description:
Policy is the topology manager policy.
"single-numa-node" enforces all resources for a pod to come from a single NUMA node.

scope.description:
Scope is the granularity at which the topology manager applies its policy: "container"
aligns each container individually, "pod" aligns all containers in a pod together. Defaults
to "container" when unset.

advancedNetworking.description:
AdvancedNetworking enables the configuration of custom networking settings for Auto nodes, such as HTTP/HTTPS proxies and no-proxy rules.
This is useful in environments with restricted internet access or specific routing requirements, allowing nodes to communicate through proxies
or bypass certain hosts and networks.

networkPolicy.description:
NetworkPolicy tells the network policy agent how it should enforce network policies against pods
By default, the Amazon VPC CNI plugin for Kubernetes configures network policies for pods in parallel with the pod provisioning
In the DefaultAllow mode, until all of the policies are configured for the new pod, containers in the new pod will start with a default allow policy.
A default allow policy means that all ingress and egress traffic is allowed to and from the new pods
In the DefaultDeny mode, a new pod will be blocked from Egress and Ingress connections till a qualifying Network Policy is applied
In this mode, you must have a network policy defined for every pod in your cluster. Host Networking pods are exempted from this requirement.

networkPolicyEventLogs.description:
NetworkPolicyEventLogs controls whether Network Policy event logging is enabled on the nodes.
By default, this value is set to Disabled. When set to Enabled, the Network Policy Agent on the node will log the outcomes of network policy decisions.

snatPolicy.description:
SNATPolicy specifies how SNAT (Source Network Address Translation) is configured on the node
If SNATPolicy is set to Disabled, the SNAT iptables rule and off-VPC IP rule are not applied, and these rules are removed if they have already been applied
Do not use SNATPolicy Disabled if you need to allow inbound communication to your pods from external VPNs, direct connections, and external VPCs,
and your pods do not need to access the Internet directly via an Internet Gateway.
If SNATPolicy is set to Random, the CNI will use PRNG, meaning that --random-fully will be added to the SNAT iptables rule
Enabling this functionality means that outbound connections will be assigned a source port that is not necessarily part of the ephemeral port range set at the OS level

capacityReservations.description:
CapacityReservations contains the current capacity reservation values that are available to this NodeClass under the
CapacityReservation selectors.

availabilityZone.description: The availability zone the capacity reservation is available in.

endTime.description:
The time at which the capacity reservation expires. Once expired, the reserved capacity is released and Karpenter
will no longer be able to launch instances into that reservation.

id.description: The id for the capacity reservation.

instanceMatchCriteria.description: Indicates the type of instance launches the capacity reservation accepts.

instanceType.description: The instance type for the capacity reservation.

interruptible.description: Indicates whether this capacity reservation is interruptible

ownerID.description: The ID of the AWS account that owns the capacity reservation.

state.description:
The state of the capacity reservation. A capacity reservation is considered to be expiring if it is within the EC2
reclaimation window. Only capacity-block reservations may be in this state.

items.description: Condition aliases the upstream type and adds additional helper methods

lastTransitionTime.description:
lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another.
This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.

message.description:
message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition.
This may be an empty string.

observedGeneration.description:
observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon.
For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date
with respect to the current state of the instance.

reason.description:
reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition.
Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field,
and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API.
The value should be a CamelCase string.
This field may not be empty.

status.description: status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.

type.description: type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.
